final_recommendation: The room converged on a surgical underwriting discipline framework: algorithmic-decision claims require independent control certification (SOC 2 or equivalent) at inception, cross-checked against auditor enforcement history, or coverage is excluded outright. The critical discovery was a systemic gate failure—renewals were accepted without auditor-history validation—triggering immediate reinsurance notification, 6-year litigation tail reserves, and mandatory hardwiring of the cross-check gate into renewal intake.
minority_objections: AI agent analyst raised concern that the governance warranty framework relies on the same control systems that failed at portfolio companies, creating circular validation risk
Emerging risk lead warned that coordinated denial messaging could still trigger narrative contagion if enforcement timing aligns with denial stagger
key_conflicts: Bridge vs. exclusion structure: whether to offer 90-day compliance bridges (creating coverage-denial traps) or exclude algorithmic decisions outright until certification clears
Denial timing: whether to stagger three fintech denials across a quarter (appearing disciplined) or disclose them simultaneously to reinsurance (revealing systemic accumulation)
Gate design vs. execution failure: whether the SOC 2 acceptance-without-validation was a one-time miss or evidence of systemic underwriting blind spots
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter abandoned the 90-day bridge structure after claims counsel demonstrated it created simultaneous claim-denial and renewal-refusal exposure
Claims counsel conceded that all three inception SOC 2s were accepted at face value without cross-checking KPMG's prior deficiency flags
Reinsurance manager accepted immediate notification of systemic gate failure rather than waiting for enforcement to surface the accumulation
red_lines: No algorithmic-decision coverage without independent control certification verified at inception—exclusion is non-negotiable
Reinsurance must be notified immediately upon discovery of systemic underwriting gaps, not after enforcement actions surface
Directors must provide written acknowledgment of algorithmic-decision exclusions with broker countersignature to prevent downstream D&O exposure
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room did not develop a concrete mechanism for monitoring live enforcement actions against auditors during denial quarters beyond manual surveillance
No discussion of how to handle clients whose boards signed governance warranties but lacked technical capacity to validate SOC 2 findings
Limited exploration of whether the auditor-history cross-check gate should apply retroactively to in-force policies or only prospectively
downstream_risk_variables: Sector-cluster accumulation caps on fintech/healthtech/crypto renewals sharing the same auditor
Litigation tail duration extended to 6+ years for 'accepted known-deficient auditor' exposure
Reinsurance XL layer accumulation triggered by correlated denials hitting same treaty simultaneously
Derivative D&O exposure when client boards signed governance representations on controls never validated by underwriting
uncertainty_notes: The room did not resolve: (1) whether the auditor-history gate failure was a design gap (systemic) or execution miss (isolated to three clients); (2) the exact population size of renewals cleared without validation in the six-month window; (3) whether KPMG's deficiency flags were publicly discoverable at inception or surfaced retroactively; (4) how to operationalize automated surveillance for live auditor enforcement actions during denial quarters.
